Fiancée got me a SteamDeck for my birthday at start of Sept, got nearly 40 games installed on it, and currently this is my most played game with over 20 hours.

This gives me what Borderlands 4 did not. Extremely addictive looter-shooter rougelike with live-service elements that constantly surprises and rewards.

Love the furry style mixed with asian mythology and unique fantasy worldbuilding. Some sick weapons. Layered & unique characters. And bot teammates is an absolute godsend feature.

There's the odd second of lag on Deck here & there, but if it does happen it's usually only when approaching the first encounter of a new room. Wish I could map the controls freely in-game (using mapping an input to R3). Sometimes there's the odd glitch or jank. And I would like to see a more in-depth online mode to easily play & interact with randoms; gifted it a friend and whilst he likes it, it's not his usual genre. Also: COSMETICS PLEASE! Character skins would be awesome.

Overall however this has become a favorite as I'm continuously learning just how much depth there is. Looking forward to more characters, weapons, maps, bosses, seasonal content, etc in the future. Thanks for your hard work devs!

(Review based on having all the DLC, unlocked all characters, completed several runs, & currently level 90)

PS. Huge props also to the community! Some great guides and fanworks out there <3
What did I even play? Ass. That's what.

There are 2 things that makes this game superior to the bajillion other co-op roguelike shooters:

1. Weapon variety. Most similar games usually have only 5-8 other weapon types where you start with 1 or 2 and the others take dozens of hours to tediously unlock. This game has over 60 weapons and you will likely unlock at least a dozen within only a couple first runs. This makes every run feel different and interesting.

2. Bot teammates. Co-op games are typically extremely grindy when playing solo so being able to add bots to your party has a very significant impact.

If there is anything I dislike about the game it would be how some bosses have that annoying mechanic where they go offscreen/invincible multiple times throughout the fight to fill the arena with mobs and reappear after killing the mobs. This a common enough mechanic in games so it might not even be worth complaining about, but it's a pet peeve of mine. It is also a bit annoying how long it takes to unlock new characters, but it's not a big problem since the gunplay matters more than the character abilities.

Honestly Gunfire Reborn is the peak of the roguelike FPS genre to me. Though I should mention that It starts off rather slow, but does pick up quite a bit by the 2nd or 3rd run.

Varied and complex characters, 70+ weapons, 200+ upgrades, it's kind of insane the amount of variety that is here. But the REAL golden piece of game design here, that keeps every run well-paced and engaging, is that at the end of every floor you ALWAYS get a core character upgrade. The pacing is genuinely the best here that I have ever seen in the genre. You always feel like you're building up and up. *Many* roguelikes, not just FPS ones, could seriously learn from this bit of design lol.

The OTHER golden piece of game design is how much you are rewarded for clever thinking in your build. The combos of upgrades and weapons can get so nuts that sometimes it will even allow you to completely negate downsides of weapons, and turn them into absolute steamrollers. (This shotgun shoots with every mouse click and release, but only has 2 shots in the magazine? But what if... what if it took its shots from my *reserve* ammo instead of the mag??? YES YOU CAN DO THAT AND IT'S INSANE)

Honestly the build complexity is SO deep that no normal run ever feels like I've quite completed a build, but being teased with that potential for perfection is what makes this game so fantastic and replayable. And there is an endless mode of course, so you do have the opportunity to refine any build to a perfect shine if you want to spend the time on it.

Multiplayer is super fun, as you can share upgrades and weapons around, meaning you're essentially all working on your own builds while helping build for each other as well. But I enjoy this a lot in singleplayer as well, since you get to just hoard all the upgrades to yourself and go wild lol.

I want to also give a special mention to the DLCs, they are all peak. 8 bucks for 2 new characters and 4 new weapons, you can get a lot of playtime out of messing around with those new options. Also, all seasons are replayable and everything is *only* obtainable via in-game progress. Each season has unique mechanics that add a whole other complex layer onto the character building. It's genuinely nuts how much there is here, and how well put together it all is.

Every weapon in this game feels distinct despite the high number of them, same for characters as well. There's a lot of charm in the presentation too, you can even use emotes as sprays which is a fun way to goof around in multiplayer. This is genuinely an exquisite game and absolutely worth your time. I think my only gripes are that I do wish the base move speed would start a bit higher to make those early runs less slow, and the translation can be wonky at times resulting in descriptions that take some effort to parse. But other than that, this is peak. The base price is already great, any sale price is practically robbery lol.
